newsitem.title: USA: Yellen sees need to raise U.S. productivity growth.
newsitem.headline: Yellen sees need to raise U.S. productivity growth.

text.p: Janet Yellen, President Clinton's nominee to chair the Council of Economic Advisers, said Wednesday that the U.S. economy is in good health but the productivity growth rate needs to be raised.
"By many measures, the economy is in very good health," Yellen said in a statement prepared for her confirmation hearing before the Senate Banking Committee.
Yellen said the "misery index," which is the sum of the inflation and unemployment rates, was at 8.3 percent in 1996, revealing that the economy is functioning well.
Throughout the long U.S. economic expansion "inflation has remained low and fallen by most broad measures," she said.
Yellen is currently a Federal Reserve governor, but did not participate in the two-day Federal Open Market Committee meeting that ends Wednesday.
She also added that consumer confidence "now stands near the highs of recent decades."
The Federal Reserve has played a positive role through its monetary policies and has kept the economy operating at its potential, Yellen said.

She pledged that if confirmed she would continue policies of the Council in the past that "facilitate the workings of the market, that emphasize the importance of incentives and efficiency, and that promote long-term growth."

One of the economic challenges that remain is to raise the rate of productivity growth above the pace that the United States has experienced since the mid 1970s, she said. "To accomplish this, our country needs to invest more -- in capital, in people and in technology," she said.
Reaching a balanced budget agreement would "facilitate faster investment in capital," Yellen said.
